A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same guard-model calibration study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains Appendix A and adds Appendix B.

before.justification: v1 reports original guard-model evaluations, calibration experiments, and diagnostic analyses in Sections 4–6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds validation-domain, prompt-length, proprietary-response, and error-rate experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The probability extraction and temperature, contextual, and batch calibration procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.1 applies existing temperature scaling with different validation data.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 extends Harmbench-adv response-source coverage to GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude-2, supplementing the ten response models in Table 2. The existing benchmarks and binary classification tasks remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated guard-model roster and temperature, contextual, and batch calibration comparators are retained. The proprietary LLMs in Appendix B.3 supply responses for evaluation; they are not additional guard-model baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds temperature fitting on 100 WildGuardMix training examples, adversarial-prompt strata of lengths below 200, 200–499, and at least 500, and FPR/FNR evaluation. These supplement the retained protocols, including the original XSTest-based temperature fitting.

E4.justification: Appendix B substantially expands diagnostic coverage: validation-domain sensitivity, possible prompt-length confounding, robustness to proprietary-model responses, and false-positive versus false-negative errors. These analyses supplement the existing jailbreak, response-model, and content-free-token investigations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these evaluations. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their values, while Tables 11–14 add substantial results on validation sensitivity, length, proprietary responses, and error direction. Table 11 reports Llama-Guard prompt ECE of 19.9% with in-domain temperature fitting alongside 26.0% with XSTest fitting. Table 13 newly reports its response ECE as 39.1%, 0.0%, and 0.8% for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude-2 respectively.

T1.justification: The calibration definition and mathematical expressions in Equations 1–6 are retained. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive mathematical definition is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the claims about overconfidence, adversarial miscalibration, response-model variability, and the benefits of contextual calibration and temperature scaling.

C2.justification: The new Limitations section makes access requirements and calibration tradeoffs explicit. Appendix B adds interpretations attributing vulnerability to adversarial content rather than length, low proprietary-response ECE to clear refusals, and higher false-negative rates to a tendency toward safe predictions.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies data-construction details for its new analyses, including the training source and size of the calibration subset and the length cutoffs. Appendix A's software, hardware, hyperparameters, truncation settings, and code/model-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on linear-probe calibration, adversarial suffix transfer, Bayesian uncertainty, and domain adaptation. These supplement the existing motivation and related-work discussion without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits, changes author order and affiliation wording, updates the conference header, and adds Limitations, Acknowledgments, and Appendix B. The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 11–14 and places Figure 2 before Table 1 on page 5, with accompanying text reflow. Existing figures and Appendix A displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The in-domain temperature comparison addresses v1's reliance on XSTest fitting, while error breakdowns and explicit limitations improve interpretation and practical guidance. The gains are limited: the length analysis does not isolate causation, and the proprietary-response evaluation omits sample counts. Overall, v2 provides useful supporting evidence without substantially revising the core study.
